children: Canadian software company Enghouse Systems hasn't made an acquisition in nearly a year, and organic growth isn't picking up the slack. RBC's Paul Treiber says 3Q will likely be below consensus expectations "due to likely continued negative organic growth and negative operating leverage." He estimates organic growth will fall by 12% in constant currency on "macro uncertainty delaying deals, reduced license and maintenance revenue from ongoing churn, and competition from vendors marketing new [artificial intelligence]-powered offerings." The analyst notes Enghouse has gone on without an acquisition in 10 months, which he says is one of the longest gaps in the company's history. (adriano.marchese@wsj.com)
